title: Blue screen of death (BSOD)
summary: A stop-code crash usually points to a driver conflict, faulty RAM, or overheating, rarely the operating system itself.
symptoms: PC crashes to a blue screen with a stop code
Happens during specific tasks (gaming, sleep/wake) or randomly
Automatic restart before you can read the code

fix_steps.title: Note the exact stop code
fix_steps.detail: Disable automatic restart (System Properties → Advanced → Startup and Recovery) so the code stays on screen, or check Event Viewer → Windows Logs → System after a crash.

fix_steps.title: Check for the obvious cause first
fix_steps.detail: Recently installed a driver, GPU, or RAM stick? Roll it back or remove it before going further.

fix_steps.title: Run a memory check
fix_steps.detail: Windows Memory Diagnostic or MemTest86 overnight; RAM faults are a top cause.

fix_steps.title: Update or roll back GPU drivers
fix_steps.detail: A clean driver reinstall (DDU + latest stable driver) resolves a large share of BSODs.

title: IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL (Stop 0x0000000A)
summary: A kernel-mode process or driver attempted to access a pageable memory address at an elevated interrupt request level (IRQL) that is strictly prohibited.
symptoms: Blue screen displaying stop code 0x0000000A or IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
Often lists a specific driver file (e.g., ntoskrnl.exe, nvlddmkm.sys, tcpip.sys)
Occurs intermittently under heavy multitasking or gaming load

fix_steps.title: Analyze the crash dump with WinDbg or BlueScreenView
fix_steps.detail: Open 'C:\Windows\Minidump' with BlueScreenView or WinDbg Preview to pinpoint the offending third-party driver module causing the invalid memory call.

fix_steps.title: Perform clean reinstall of graphics and network drivers
fix_steps.detail: Display and network adapters are the most frequent culprits. Download latest WHQL certified drivers from vendor websites and perform a clean install.

fix_steps.title: Verify memory stability with Windows Memory Diagnostic
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+R, type 'mdsched.exe', select 'Restart now and check for problems' to test for defective RAM cells.

fix_steps.title: Disable aggressive CPU/RAM overclocks
fix_steps.detail: Reset XMP/EXPO profiles in BIOS to base JEDEC clock speeds to test if memory timing instability is throwing memory access violations.

title: PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA (Stop 0x00000050)
summary: The system attempted to reference nonexistent physical memory, typically indicating a failing RAM stick, bad L2/L3 CPU cache, or a corrupt NTFS volume.
symptoms: Stop code 0x00000050 on blue screen
Crashes immediately upon waking from sleep or booting up
Occurs after installing a new RAM module or expansion card

fix_steps.title: Run MemTest86 on each RAM stick individually
fix_steps.detail: Create a bootable MemTest86 USB drive and test one stick at a time. A single error in Test 6 or 8 confirms hardware memory replacement is needed.

fix_steps.title: Run CHKDSK to repair filesystem metadata
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run 'chkdsk C: /f /r'. Reboot to let Windows scan nonpaged storage blocks.

fix_steps.title: Recreate the Windows Pagefile
fix_steps.detail: Go to System Properties → Advanced → Performance Settings → Advanced → Change Virtual Memory. Set to 'No paging file', reboot, and reset to 'System managed size' to discard corrupted pagefile blocks.

fix_steps.title: Disable third-party antivirus suites
fix_steps.detail: Third-party kernel-level antivirus drivers frequently trigger nonpaged memory faults. Temporarily uninstall to isolate.

title: SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION (Stop 0x0000003B)
summary: An unhandled exception occurred during the execution of a system service routine, frequently caused by graphics drivers or anticheat software.
symptoms: Stop code 0x0000003B with parameters
Commonly references win32kbase.sys, dxgkrnl.sys, or EasyAntiCheat.sys
Crashes while launching or alt-tabbing out of 3D games

fix_steps.title: Update graphics drivers with a clean installation
fix_steps.detail: Use Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) in Safe Mode, then install the latest WHQL release for your GPU.

fix_steps.title: Update game anticheat software
fix_steps.detail: Anticheat software (Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, Vanguard) running at kernel level can crash when conflicting with Windows updates. Verify game files on Steam/Epic to reinstall anticheat.

fix_steps.title: Scan and restore system files with SFC and DISM
fix_steps.detail: Run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' followed by 'sfc /scannow' in an elevated terminal to repair corrupted system DLLs.

fix_steps.title: Disable GPU hardware acceleration in apps
fix_steps.detail: Turn off hardware acceleration in Discord, Spotify, and Chrome if crashes occur during media playback.

title: KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR (Stop 0x0000007A)
summary: The operating system kernel failed to read requested kernel data from disk storage into physical RAM due to hardware connection failure or bad sectors.
symptoms: Stop code 0x0000007A with status codes like 0xC000009C (bad sector) or 0xC000009D (disconnected device)
System freezes completely before blue screen appears
Drive disappears from Windows File Explorer after crash

fix_steps.title: Inspect SSD / HDD health with CrystalDiskInfo
fix_steps.detail: Check SMART attributes. Look for Reallocated Sectors, Current Pending Sectors, or Uncorrectable Error Count. Any non-zero count warns of drive degradation.

fix_steps.title: Reseat NVMe M.2 SSD or SATA cables
fix_steps.detail: Turn off power, remove the M.2 SSD, clean the contacts, and firmly reinstall. For 2.5"/3.5" SATA drives, replace the SATA data cable and try another motherboard port.

fix_steps.title: Update SSD firmware
fix_steps.detail: Open your drive manufacturer's software (Samsung Magician, WD Dashboard, Crucial Storage Executive) and apply pending firmware updates.

fix_steps.title: Run CHKDSK /F /R
fix_steps.detail: Execute 'chkdsk /f /r' from an elevated prompt to flag and isolate damaged filesystem sectors.

title: CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED (Stop 0x000000EF)
summary: An essential Windows system process (such as csrss.exe, wininit.exe, or svchost.exe) unexpectedly terminated, forcing an immediate safety kernel panic.
symptoms: Sudden blue screen displaying CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED
Crash dump file fails to save or stays stuck at 0%
System reboots into BIOS or displays 'No bootable device found'

fix_steps.title: Check SSD health and connections immediately
fix_steps.detail: When an SSD drops off the PCIe/SATA bus, Windows cannot read critical system files, causing csrss.exe to terminate. Reseat the SSD and check SMART logs.

fix_steps.title: Repair system file corruption
fix_steps.detail: Open administrative PowerShell and run: 'sfc /scannow'. If violations are found and repaired, reboot and verify stability.

fix_steps.title: Use System Restore to roll back recent changes
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+R, run 'rstrui.exe', and select a restore point created prior to the first occurrence of the crash.

fix_steps.title: Check for malware infections
fix_steps.detail: Run a full scan with Microsoft Defender Offline scan to ensure malware has not hooked or injected malicious code into svchost.exe.

title: SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED (Stop 0x0000007E)
summary: A system thread generated an exception that the kernel error handler did not catch, predominantly caused by outdated hardware device drivers.
symptoms: Stop code 0x0000007E, often naming files like nvlddmkm.sys, atikmdag.sys, or RTKVHD64.sys
Repeated blue screen reboots during Windows startup
Occurs following a Windows Update or driver installation

fix_steps.title: Identify the driver filename listed on the blue screen
fix_steps.detail: Note the '.sys' file listed below the stop code. For example, nvlddmkm.sys is Nvidia, atikmdag.sys is AMD, and netwtw10.sys is Intel Wi-Fi.

fix_steps.title: Boot into Safe Mode and roll back driver
fix_steps.detail: Boot into Windows Safe Mode, open Device Manager, right-click the corresponding hardware device, select Properties → Driver tab → Roll Back Driver.

fix_steps.title: Reinstall latest chipset and BIOS firmware
fix_steps.detail: Download latest motherboard chipset INF drivers and audio drivers directly from the manufacturer motherboard support page.

fix_steps.title: Run DISM image repair
fix_steps.detail: Execute 'dism /online /cleanup-image /restorehealth' in Command Prompt to fix corrupted system driver stores.

title: DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION (Stop 0x00000133)
summary: The Deferred Procedure Call (DPC) watchdog timer detected a single DPC routine that ran for excessive duration or spent too long at high IRQL.
symptoms: Stop code 0x00000133 on crash screen
Cursor freezes completely for 5-10 seconds before BSOD triggers
Common on SSDs using standard Microsoft SATA AHCI driver

fix_steps.title: Change SATA AHCI Controller driver in Device Manager
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager → expand 'IDE ATA/ATAPI controllers'. If 'Standard SATA AHCI Controller' is listed, right-click → Update driver → Browse my computer → Let me pick → choose vendor driver or verify driver compatibility.

fix_steps.title: Update SSD firmware
fix_steps.detail: Outdated solid-state drive firmware is the leading trigger for DPC watchdog timeouts. Use manufacturer utilities to flash latest SSD firmware.

fix_steps.title: Update Wi-Fi and Bluetooth drivers
fix_steps.detail: Wireless adapters can hold DPC queues open if packet handshakes hang. Download the latest drivers from Intel or Qualcomm.

fix_steps.title: Check system DPC latency with LatencyMon
fix_steps.detail: Run the free LatencyMon utility to detect which specific driver generates execution times over 1000 microseconds.

title: DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE (Stop 0x0000009F)
summary: A device driver was unable to transition between active and power-saving states (sleep, hibernation, or resume) within the kernel timeout window.
symptoms: Stop code 0x0000009F appears when waking PC from sleep or closing laptop lid
PC hangs indefinitely on 'Shutting down' or 'Restarting' screen
Laptop battery drains rapidly while asleep

fix_steps.title: Disable Fast Startup in Windows
fix_steps.detail: Go to Control Panel → Power Options → Choose what the power buttons do → click 'Change settings that are currently unavailable' → uncheck 'Turn on fast startup'.

fix_steps.title: Update Intel Management Engine (ME) or AMD Chipset drivers
fix_steps.detail: Power-state transition commands depend on chipset firmware. Install the latest official chipset drivers for your motherboard.

fix_steps.title: Set PCIe Link State Power Management to Off
fix_steps.detail: In Control Panel → Power Options → Edit Plan Settings → Change advanced power settings → expand 'PCI Express' → Link State Power Management → set to 'Off'.

fix_steps.title: Update GPU and USB controller drivers
fix_steps.detail: Ensure third-party USB hubs or external docks have up-to-date firmware that supports ACPI D3 sleep states.

title: WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR (Stop 0x00000124)
summary: Windows Hardware Error Architecture (WHEA) detected a physical hardware error that cannot be corrected by CPU or bus architecture.
symptoms: Stop code 0x00000124 on crash screen
Immediate reboot without writing dump file (0% progress)
Triggered by high CPU/GPU loads or extreme thermal spikes

fix_steps.title: Remove CPU undervolts or overclocks
fix_steps.detail: Enter BIOS and reset CPU Vcore, Load-Line Calibration (LLC), and PBO/Curve Optimizer settings to factory defaults. Insufficient core voltage is the #1 cause of WHEA errors.

fix_steps.title: Monitor CPU and VRM temperatures
fix_steps.detail: Use HWInfo64 to ensure CPU temperature is below 90°C and motherboard VRMs are not thermal throttling under load.

fix_steps.title: Update motherboard BIOS for microcode patches
fix_steps.detail: Motherboard vendors release BIOS updates containing Intel/AMD CPU microcode stability fixes to resolve internal bus parity errors.

fix_steps.title: Test with an alternate power supply
fix_steps.detail: Transient voltage dips from a failing or underpowered PSU trigger internal CPU power-plane resets.

title: MEMORY_MANAGEMENT (Stop 0x0000001A)
summary: The Windows memory manager encountered severe corruption in its internal page translation tables or physical memory structures.
symptoms: Stop code 0x0000001A with subtype parameters
Web browser tabs crash frequently with 'STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION'
Large file decompression (.zip, game updates) throws CRC errors

fix_steps.title: Test RAM with MemTest86
fix_steps.detail: Boot to a MemTest86 flash drive and run a minimum of 4 passes. Any red errors indicate a defective physical RAM stick that must be replaced.

fix_steps.title: Disable XMP/EXPO memory profiles in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: High-frequency DDR4 (3600MHz+) and DDR5 (6000MHz+) overclock profiles can destabilize the integrated memory controller (IMC). Run at stock JEDEC speeds to test.

fix_steps.title: Reseat RAM sticks in slots A2 and B2
fix_steps.detail: Ensure modules are installed in the second and fourth slots from the CPU socket, and contacts are free of dust.

fix_steps.title: Run System File Checker
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run 'sfc /scannow' to fix system files corrupted by memory write errors.

title: KMODE_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED (Stop 0x0000001E)
summary: A kernel-mode program generated an exception that the error handler was unable to process, typically due to faulty drivers or memory corruption.
symptoms: Stop code 0x0000001E on blue screen
Often mentions a driver such as ndis.sys, tcpip.sys, or athw8x.sys
Occurs during networking activity or peripheral plugging

fix_steps.title: Note the exact driver name on the crash screen
fix_steps.detail: If a driver is listed in parentheses after the stop code, boot to Safe Mode and uninstall or update that specific device driver.

fix_steps.title: Turn off Fast Startup
fix_steps.detail: Fast Startup saves kernel sessions to disk and can reload corrupted kernel memory states. Disable it in Power Options.

fix_steps.title: Run Driver Verifier to catch faulty third-party drivers
fix_steps.detail: Press Win+R, run 'verifier', create standard settings for all third-party drivers, and reboot. (Warning: know how to boot Safe Mode to turn Verifier off).

fix_steps.title: Test memory with Windows Memory Diagnostic
fix_steps.detail: Hardware memory defects frequently disguise themselves as unhandled kernel exceptions.

title: CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT (Stop 0x00000101)
summary: An expected clock interrupt on a secondary processor core was not delivered within the allocated time interval, pointing to CPU core lockup or instability.
symptoms: Stop code 0x00000101 on blue screen
System completely freezes; mouse cursor stops moving instantly
Sound buzzes violently through speakers or headphones

fix_steps.title: Reset BIOS settings to factory defaults
fix_steps.detail: Clear all CPU multiplier adjustments, manual voltages, and power limits in BIOS to verify stock processor stability.

fix_steps.title: Update motherboard BIOS firmware
fix_steps.detail: Motherboard manufacturers release updated AGESA (AMD) or microcode (Intel) firmware specifically addressing inter-core communication deadlocks.

fix_steps.title: Check CPU operating temperature and mounting pressure
fix_steps.detail: Extreme core temperatures (>100°C) or uneven cooler bracket mounting pressure can cause CPU cores to hang.

fix_steps.title: Run Intel Processor Diagnostic Tool or Prime95
fix_steps.detail: Stress test individual CPU cores. If a specific core consistently halts while others continue, the CPU has a degraded physical core and requires RMA.

title: KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE (Stop 0x00000139)
summary: The operating system kernel detected corruption of critical kernel structures, indicating a driver or program violated kernel data integrity.
symptoms: Stop code 0x00000139 on blue screen
Occurs when opening specific games, VPN software, or virtualization tools
System crashes after installing recent security patches

fix_steps.title: Uninstall recently added third-party software
fix_steps.detail: Virtual drive emulators, RGB control software, and outdated VPN clients frequently modify kernel structures. Uninstall them in Windows Settings.

fix_steps.title: Run SFC and DISM repair scans
fix_steps.detail: Open an elevated Command Prompt and run 'sfc /scannow' to verify kernel binary integrity.

fix_steps.title: Update motherboard BIOS and chipset drivers
fix_steps.detail: Security checks can fail if processor virtualization extensions (Intel VT-x / AMD-V) behave erratically on outdated firmware.

fix_steps.title: Perform clean boot to isolate startup services
fix_steps.detail: Open 'msconfig', go to Services tab, check 'Hide all Microsoft services', click 'Disable all', and reboot to isolate conflicting background drivers.

title: BAD_POOL_HEADER (Stop 0x00000019)
summary: A device driver improperly allocated memory in the kernel pool, resulting in a corrupted memory allocation header.
symptoms: Stop code 0x00000019 appears unexpectedly
Crashes when writing to external drives or transferring large files
Multiple applications crash with memory read errors

fix_steps.title: Disconnect recently connected external hardware
fix_steps.detail: Unplug third-party USB hubs, external capture cards, and Wi-Fi dongles to determine if a driver allocated malformed pool memory.

fix_steps.title: Update network and storage controller drivers
fix_steps.detail: Network adapter drivers are the most frequent source of bad pool allocation calls. Install latest manufacturer drivers.

fix_steps.title: Test RAM with MemTest86
fix_steps.detail: Faulty physical memory addresses can corrupt pool headers as data is written.

fix_steps.title: Disable third-party antivirus suites
fix_steps.detail: Real-time filesystem filter drivers from third-party security software can corrupt pool headers during deep file inspection.

title: DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL (Stop 0x000000D1)
summary: A named kernel-mode driver attempted to access pageable memory at an improper IRQL level, identifying the driver at fault.
symptoms: Stop code 0x000000D1 clearly displaying the driver filename on screen
Common files: storport.sys, netwtw08.sys, nvlddmkm.sys
Crashes while streaming video or heavy network downloading

fix_steps.title: Identify and reinstall the offending driver
fix_steps.detail: Search the filename shown on the crash screen. If it belongs to your Wi-Fi, Ethernet, audio, or GPU, download a clean installer from the vendor and reinstall.

fix_steps.title: Roll back to previous stable driver in Device Manager
fix_steps.detail: If the crash started after a recent driver update, open Device Manager → right-click device → Properties → Driver → Roll Back Driver.

fix_steps.title: Run System File Checker
fix_steps.detail: Execute 'sfc /scannow' in administrative Command Prompt to restore any damaged core Windows networking or storage components.

fix_steps.title: Disable network adapter energy efficient features
fix_steps.detail: In Device Manager → Network adapters → right-click your adapter → Advanced → disable 'Energy Efficient Ethernet' and 'Green Ethernet'.

title: BSOD: DXGKRNL_FATAL_ERROR (0x00000113)
summary: The DirectX Graphics Kernel subsystem detects a fatal violation, typically triggered by an unstable GPU memory overclock, corrupt display driver, or failing PCIe power delivery.
symptoms: Blue screen displaying stop code: DXGKRNL_FATAL_ERROR
Screen freezes or turns black for 3 seconds before blue screen
Occurs while playing 3D DirectX 12 games or rendering in Premiere

fix_steps.title: Clean reinstall GPU driver with Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU)
fix_steps.detail: Download DDU and the latest driver package from NVIDIA or AMD. Boot Windows into Safe Mode, run DDU to completely strip graphics drivers, restart, and perform a clean install.

fix_steps.title: Disable GPU VRAM and Core Overclock in MSI Afterburner
fix_steps.detail: Open MSI Afterburner or AMD Adrenalin. Reset Core Clock and Memory Clock offsets to factory +0 MHz and disable any custom undervolting profiles.

fix_steps.title: Verify PCIe power cables are dedicated (not daisy-chained)
fix_steps.detail: Ensure each 8-pin PCIe power connector on your graphics card runs a separate, dedicated cable directly from the power supply unit rather than sharing a pigtail splitter.

fix_steps.title: Run DirectX End-User Runtime installer
fix_steps.detail: Download and run the Microsoft DirectX End-User Runtime installer to repair missing or corrupted legacy DirectX binaries in C:\Windows\System32.

title: BSOD: VIDEO_SCHEDULER_INTERNAL_ERROR (0x00000119)
summary: The Windows GPU video scheduler detects that a display driver timed out while executing a graphics command and could not be recovered via Timeout Detection and Recovery (TDR).
symptoms: Stop code 0x00000119: VIDEO_SCHEDULER_INTERNAL_ERROR
Frequent display driver crashes when watching YouTube or hardware-accelerated video
Audio loops in a buzzing sound right before the crash

fix_steps.title: Turn off Hardware Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS)
fix_steps.detail: Go to Windows Settings > System > Display > Graphics > Change default graphics settings. Toggle 'Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling' to Off and reboot your PC.

fix_steps.title: Disable browser hardware acceleration as a test
fix_steps.detail: In Chrome, Edge, or Discord, open Settings > System and turn off 'Use graphics acceleration when available'. If crashes halt, the graphics driver video decode engine is unstable.

fix_steps.title: Roll back to previous WHQL Studio or Game Ready driver
fix_steps.detail: Open Device Manager > Display adapters > Right-click your GPU > Properties > Driver tab > Click 'Roll Back Driver' if the issue began immediately after a recent driver update.

fix_steps.title: Repair corrupted Windows system files with SFC and DISM
fix_steps.detail: Open Terminal as Administrator and execute: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth followed by sfc /scannow to fix damaged graphics subsystem components.

title: BSOD: PFN_LIST_CORRUPT (0x0000004E)
summary: The Page Frame Number (PFN) list, an internal operating system structure used to map physical memory addresses, became corrupted due to faulty RAM chips or disk I/O driver errors.
symptoms: Stop code: PFN_LIST_CORRUPT (0x0000004E)
Crash occurs randomly during web browsing, file copying, or gaming
Chkdsk finds indexing discrepancies on the system drive

fix_steps.title: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic tool
fix_steps.detail: Press Win + R, type 'mdsched.exe', and select 'Restart now and check for problems'. Allow the standard test pass to complete; if any hardware errors are found, RAM is defective.

fix_steps.title: Test memory sticks individually in slot A2
fix_steps.detail: Power off the PC. Remove all RAM modules except one in the primary slot (usually A2). Test each stick one at a time to identify the specific failing physical module.

fix_steps.title: Disable aggressive RAM XMP / EXPO / DOCP profile
fix_steps.detail: Reboot into BIOS and disable memory overclocking, letting RAM operate at base JEDEC speed (e.g. 4800 MHz DDR5 or 2133/2400 MHz DDR4) to test controller stability.

fix_steps.title: Run CHKDSK to repair bad filesystem sectors
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Admin and execute: chkdsk C: /f /r. Type Y to schedule at next boot, restart the PC, and allow Windows to relocate data away from damaged storage clusters.

title: BSOD: BAD_OBJECT_HEADER (0x00000189)
summary: The Windows kernel executive found that an internal object header was corrupted, almost always caused by a misbehaved third-party driver overwriting kernel memory pools.
symptoms: Stop code 0x00000189: BAD_OBJECT_HEADER
Bugcheck occurs during shutdown, sleep, or wake transition
Minidump points to ntoskrnl.exe or a third-party .sys driver

fix_steps.title: Analyze minidump with BlueScreenView or WinDbg
fix_steps.detail: Download free BlueScreenView or Microsoft WinDbg from Microsoft Store. Open the crash dump in C:\Windows\Minidump to identify the exact third-party driver filename (e.g. AsIO.sys, CorsairVBus.sys).

fix_steps.title: Uninstall conflicting RGB, tuning, or anti-virus utilities
fix_steps.detail: Software like ASUS Armoury Crate, Corsair iCUE, Razer Synapse, or third-party firewalls install deep kernel drivers that frequently corrupt object memory. Uninstall them to test stability.

fix_steps.title: Update all motherboard chipset and serial IO drivers
fix_steps.detail: Download the latest AMD Chipset Drivers or Intel Management Engine (ME) and Serial IO drivers from your motherboard support page.

fix_steps.title: Run Driver Verifier to isolate the offending driver
fix_steps.detail: Press Win + R, type 'verifier', choose 'Create standard settings' > 'Select driver names from a list', check all non-Microsoft drivers, reboot, and observe which driver triggers an immediate pinpoint BSOD.

title: BSOD: KERNEL_MODE_HEAP_CORRUPTION (0x0000013A)
summary: A kernel-mode driver corrupted the operating system kernel heap memory manager, commonly triggered by kernel-level gaming anti-cheat engines or outdated network filter drivers.
symptoms: Stop code 0x0000013A: KERNEL_MODE_HEAP_CORRUPTION
Crash happens upon launching Valorant (Vanguard), Fortnite (Easy Anti-Cheat), or Call of Duty (Ricochet)
Minidump blames vgk.sys, easyanticheat.sys, or e1d.sys

fix_steps.title: Reinstall game anti-cheat service
fix_steps.detail: Uninstall the game anti-cheat from Control Panel (e.g. Riot Vanguard or EasyAntiCheat). Launch the game launcher as Administrator to trigger a fresh, clean anti-cheat installation.

fix_steps.title: Update Wi-Fi and Ethernet network adapter drivers
fix_steps.detail: Packet filtering drivers installed by network cards (like Intel Killer Suite or Realtek Dragon) frequently corrupt kernel memory. Download pure bare-metal INF drivers and uninstall the bloatware control center.

fix_steps.title: Enable Core Isolation / Memory Integrity in Windows Security
fix_steps.detail: Open Windows Security > Device Security > Core isolation details > Turn on 'Memory Integrity' (HVCI). This forces Windows to isolate kernel processes and block insecure drivers.

fix_steps.title: Repair corrupt Windows system files with DISM
fix_steps.detail: Run: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth in PowerShell as Administrator to replace corrupted kernel memory libraries.

title: BSOD: HYPERVISOR_ERROR (0x00020001)
summary: The Windows Hyper-V hypervisor encountered an unrecoverable exception, typically caused by conflicting third-party virtualization software (VirtualBox, VMware) or unstable CPU voltage.
symptoms: Stop code: HYPERVISOR_ERROR (0x00020001)
Occurs when launching WSL2, Windows Sandbox, or Docker Desktop
System hangs or reboots during virtualization workloads

fix_steps.title: Verify CPU Virtualization (SVM / Intel VT-x) is enabled in BIOS
fix_steps.detail: Enter BIOS setup, open Advanced CPU Configuration, and confirm that 'Intel Virtualization Technology' (VT-x) or AMD 'SVM Mode' is set to Enabled.

fix_steps.title: Disable conflicting third-party virtualization hypervisors
fix_steps.detail: If VMware Workstation or Oracle VirtualBox is installed, update them to versions that support the Windows Hypervisor Platform (WHPX) API, or uninstall them temporarily.

fix_steps.title: Update WSL2 Linux kernel package
fix_steps.detail: Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run: wsl --update followed by wsl --shutdown to refresh the Hyper-V microcode container.

fix_steps.title: Reset CPU curve optimizer / undervolt settings
fix_steps.detail: Aggressive negative CPU Curve Optimizer (PBO) offsets frequently pass standard stress tests but fail under the nested virtualization context switching of Hyper-V. Reset offset to 0.

title: BSOD: DRIVER_VERIFIER_DETECTED_VIOLATION (0x000000C4)
summary: Windows Driver Verifier caught an active device driver performing an illegal operation, such as accessing paged memory at elevated IRQL or freeing already-released memory.
symptoms: Stop code: DRIVER_VERIFIER_DETECTED_VIOLATION (0x000000C4)
Names the failing driver file directly on the blue screen (e.g., driver.sys)
PC gets stuck in a blue screen boot loop until Safe Mode is accessed

fix_steps.title: Boot into Safe Mode and turn off Driver Verifier
fix_steps.detail: When Windows fails to boot twice, enter the Automatic Repair screen > Troubleshoot > Advanced Options > Startup Settings > Restart > Press 4 for Safe Mode. Open Command Prompt as Admin and execute: verifier /reset.

fix_steps.title: Identify the driver filename shown on the crash screen
fix_steps.detail: Note the .sys file referenced on the blue screen (or inspect C:\Windows\MEMORY.DMP with BlueScreenView). Search the filename online to identify the associated hardware or software.

fix_steps.title: Update or uninstall the identified software or driver
fix_steps.detail: In Safe Mode, open Device Manager or Control Panel and update the hardware driver or uninstall the utility responsible for the flagged .sys file.

fix_steps.title: Restart PC in normal mode
fix_steps.detail: Reboot the PC normally. Verifier is now disabled, and the offending driver is either updated or removed.

title: BSOD: SYSTEM_PTE_MISUSE (0x000000DA)
summary: A driver attempted an illegal operation against Page Table Entries (PTEs) or conflicting memory protection flags, often triggered by outdated security software or firmware bugs.
symptoms: Stop code 0x000000DA: SYSTEM_PTE_MISUSE
Occurs during high memory pressure or intensive data streaming
System logs event ID 1001 in Windows Event Viewer

fix_steps.title: Update motherboard BIOS firmware
fix_steps.detail: System PTE tracking is heavily tied to motherboard ACPI tables and memory mapping registers. Download and flash the latest UEFI release from the manufacturer.

fix_steps.title: Check for incompatible third-party antivirus filters
fix_steps.detail: Uninstall legacy antivirus or security tools (such as older Avast, AVG, or McAfee suites) using their official cleanup removal utilities.

fix_steps.title: Verify Windows system files with System File Checker
fix_steps.detail: Run: sfc /scannow in an elevated Command Prompt to restore damaged memory management system binaries.

fix_steps.title: Reset Windows Virtual Memory paging file configuration
fix_steps.detail: Open SystemPropertiesPerformance.exe > Advanced tab > Virtual Memory Change > Check 'Automatically manage paging file size for all drives' > Click OK and restart.

title: WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR (0x00000124) hardware CPU or PCIe crash
summary: Hardware error detected by Windows Hardware Error Architecture (WHEA) caused by unstable CPU voltage, bad undervolt, or PCIe fault.
symptoms: Blue screen stop code: WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR
Bugcheck parameter 1 = 0x00000000 (Machine Check Exception)
Crashes under gaming load or when idle after overclocking or undervolting

fix_steps.title: Reset all CPU Curve Optimizer and undervolts to stock in BIOS
fix_steps.instruction: Enter BIOS and reset CPU voltage settings to factory stock. If using AMD Curve Optimizer or Intel Voltage Offset, set to 0. A negative curve that is unstable at light loads causes immediate WHEA crashes.
fix_steps.caution: Negative core offsets that pass 100% stress tests often crash when cores drop to low idle frequencies.

fix_steps.title: Inspect WHEA record in Event Viewer (Event ID 18/19)
fix_steps.instruction: Open Windows Event Viewer -> Windows Logs -> System. Filter by Event Source 'WHEA-Logger'. Look for Event ID 18 (Machine Check Exception) and note the 'APIC ID' to determine which specific CPU core failed.
fix_steps.caution: APIC ID 0/1 = Core 0; APIC ID 2/3 = Core 1.

fix_steps.title: Update motherboard BIOS for CPU microcode stability
fix_steps.instruction: Ensure motherboard BIOS is updated. Both Intel 13th/14th Gen (0x129 microcode) and AMD Ryzen 7000/9000 series rely on critical AGESA BIOS microcode updates to prevent voltage degradation crashes.
fix_steps.caution: Never interrupt power during a BIOS flash.

title: KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE (0x00000139) anti-cheat or memory crash
summary: Windows kernel integrity check failed, typically caused by kernel-level anti-cheat drivers (Vanguard, BattlEye, EAC) or faulty RAM.
symptoms: Stop code KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE
Crashes while playing Valorant, Rainbow Six Siege, or Easy Anti-Cheat games
Crash dump references vgk.sys, bedaisy.sys, or easyanticheat.sys

fix_steps.title: Reinstall clean Anti-Cheat service
fix_steps.instruction: Uninstall the offending anti-cheat (e.g. Riot Vanguard) from Windows Apps & Features. Delete its leftover program directory in 'C:\Program Files\Riot Vanguard'. Reboot PC, then launch game client to reinstall fresh service.
fix_steps.caution: Ensure Windows Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) and Core Isolation are supported in Windows Security settings.

fix_steps.title: Test memory integrity with Windows Memory Diagnostic
fix_steps.instruction: Press Win+R, type 'mdsched.exe' and choose 'Restart now and check for problems'. If memory errors are reported, run MemTest86 on a bootable USB to pinpoint failing RAM modules.
fix_steps.caution: Even 1 single memory error will corrupt kernel security checksums.

fix_steps.title: Run DISM and SFC scans to verify kernel integrity
fix_steps.instruction: Open Terminal as Administrator. Run 'DISM.exe /Online /Cleanup-image /Restorehealth' followed by 'sfc /scannow' to repair damaged system DLL files.
fix_steps.caution: Reboot PC once repairs are reported.

title: CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED (0x000000EF) NVMe SSD dropping or Windows system crash
summary: Essential Windows background process terminated abruptly, often caused by an M.2 NVMe SSD suddenly dropping off the PCIe bus.
symptoms: Blue screen stop code: CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED
BSOD dump creation gets stuck at 0% and fails to write minidump
After rebooting, PC enters BIOS directly because SSD is not detected until power cycle

fix_steps.title: Reseat NVMe M.2 SSD in motherboard slot
fix_steps.instruction: Shut down PC and unplug power cord. Unscrew M.2 heatsink, remove M.2 SSD, clean gold contacts gently with a dry lint-free cloth, and reinsert firmly into M.2 slot at a 30-degree angle. Screw down securely.
fix_steps.caution: Thermal expansion and contraction can cause slight contact oxidation in M.2 slots over time.

fix_steps.title: Update NVMe SSD firmware via vendor utility
fix_steps.instruction: Download vendor SSD management software (Samsung Magician, WD Dashboard, Crucial Storage Executive, Kingston SSD Manager). Check for and apply SSD firmware updates.
fix_steps.caution: Samsung 980/990 Pro and WD SN850X had known firmware bugs causing SSDs to lock into read-only mode or disconnect under PCIe 4.0 sleep states.

fix_steps.title: Disable PCI Express Link State Power Management
fix_steps.instruction: Open 'powercfg.cpl' -> Change plan settings -> Change advanced power settings. Expand 'PCI Express' -> 'Link State Power Management' -> set to 'Off'.
fix_steps.caution: Prevents Windows from putting NVMe controller into ultra-low-power states that fail to wake up in time.

title: SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED (0x0000007E) driver crash on boot
summary: System thread generated an unhandled exception, pointing directly to a specific third-party .sys driver file on the blue screen.
symptoms: Stop code: SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED
Blue screen mentions filename: nvlddmkm.sys, atikmdag.sys, rtpx64.sys, or netwtw10.sys
Occurs in a boot loop or immediately when opening 3D programs

fix_steps.title: Note the exact .sys filename displayed on the BSOD screen
fix_steps.instruction: The filename identifies the faulty component: nvlddmkm.sys (Nvidia GPU), atikmdag.sys (AMD GPU), rtpx64.sys (Realtek Audio), netwtw10.sys (Intel Wi-Fi).
fix_steps.caution: If no filename is listed, check C:\Windows\Minidump with BlueScreenView.

fix_steps.title: Boot into Safe Mode and roll back or uninstall the driver
fix_steps.instruction: Hold Shift while clicking Restart -> Troubleshoot -> Advanced options -> Startup Settings -> Restart -> press 4 for Safe Mode. Open Device Manager -> locate the device matching the driver -> right-click Properties -> Driver tab -> 'Roll Back Driver' (or Uninstall Device).
fix_steps.caution: Safe Mode loads basic generic drivers, allowing you to bypass the crash.

fix_steps.title: Disable Fast Startup in Windows Power Options
fix_steps.instruction: Press Win+R, type 'powercfg.cpl' -> click 'Choose what the power buttons do' -> click 'Change settings that are currently unavailable' -> uncheck 'Turn on fast startup'. Click Save changes.
fix_steps.caution: Fast Startup saves corrupted driver kernel state to disk on shutdown, causing repeated boot loops.

title: PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA (0x00000050) invalid memory address crash
summary: Invalid system memory referenced, usually caused by defective RAM hardware, bad memory timings, or corrupted NTFS volume.
symptoms: Blue screen stop code: PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA
Random crashes happening at different times and in different applications
Google Chrome tabs crashing frequently with 'STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION' or 'Out of Memory'

fix_steps.title: Test RAM with 1 stick at a time to find the defective module
fix_steps.instruction: Turn off PC and unplug power. Remove all RAM sticks except 1 stick in slot 2 (A2). Use PC. If stable, swap in the second stick. A single bad memory chip on a RAM stick will trigger random page fault crashes.
fix_steps.caution: Handle RAM sticks by the plastic edges, never touch gold contact pins directly.

fix_steps.title: Disable aggressive RAM XMP / EXPO overclock in BIOS
fix_steps.instruction: Reboot into BIOS setup (tap Del/F2). Disable XMP or set DRAM Frequency to JEDEC base spec (2133MHz or 4800MHz). If the blue screens stop, your memory controller requires slightly higher SoC voltage or updated BIOS microcode.
fix_steps.caution: High-speed RAM (DDR5-6400+) requires manual voltage tuning on 4-stick configurations.

fix_steps.title: Run check disk with bad sector recovery
fix_steps.instruction: Open Command Prompt as Administrator. Type: 'chkdsk C: /f /r' and press Enter. Type 'Y' to schedule disk check on next restart. Reboot PC.
fix_steps.caution: Scans pagefile.sys filesystem sectors and repairs bad NTFS index records.

title: DRIVER_VERIFIER_DETECTED_VIOLATION (0x000000C4) Windows Driver Verifier boot loop
summary: PC is stuck in an infinite blue screen restart loop after running Windows Driver Verifier tool (verifier.exe).
symptoms: PC crashes with DRIVER_VERIFIER_DETECTED_VIOLATION within 5 seconds of Windows loading
User ran 'verifier.exe' following bad online forum advice and is now locked out
Infinite automatic repair boot loop

fix_steps.title: Enter Safe Mode to disable Driver Verifier flags
fix_steps.instruction: Force power off PC twice during Windows logo boot until 'Automatic Repair' appears. Click Advanced options -> Troubleshoot -> Advanced options -> Startup Settings -> Restart -> press 4 for Safe Mode.
fix_steps.caution: Driver Verifier will not enforce memory checks in Safe Mode.

fix_steps.title: Reset and disable Driver Verifier completely
fix_steps.instruction: Once in Safe Mode, press Win+X -> Command Prompt (Admin). Type: 'verifier /reset' and hit Enter. Verify output says 'No settings were changed' or 'Settings were reset'.
fix_steps.caution: Never use Driver Verifier unless you are an experienced software kernel developer debugging code.

fix_steps.title: Delete verifier registry keys if reset command fails
fix_steps.instruction: In Admin Command Prompt, run: 'reg delete "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v VerifyDrivers /f' and 'reg delete "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management" /v VerifyDriverLevel /f'. Reboot PC.
fix_steps.caution: PC will now boot straight to normal Windows desktop.
